items.task_prompt: Write `uart_divisor`, which returns the baud divisor to program for the given source clock and baud rate. The divisor register is rounded to the nearest integer.
spec_facts: The divisor is the nearest integer to src_hz / (16 * baud).
items.preamble:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SpecGap(pub &'static str);
items.fn_signature: pub fn uart_divisor(src_hz: u32, baud: u32) -> Result<u32, SpecGap>

items.task_prompt: Write `pack_desc`, which builds the 32-bit descriptor word from a length, a channel number and a flag set.
items.fn_signature: pub fn pack_desc(len: u16, chan: u8, flags: u16) -> Result<u32, SpecGap>

items.task_prompt: Write `enable_crc_offload`, which turns on the hardware CRC offload.
spec_facts: The spec repository does not describe CRC offload; the source document says: write 1 to the register at 0x28.
items.fn_signature: pub fn enable_crc_offload<B: RegBus>(bus: &mut B) -> Result<(), SpecGap>

items.task_prompt: Write `clear_error`, which clears the error flag in STATUS (offset 0x10) and leaves the done flag alone. Caller's note: // the error flag is bit 2 (0x4) of STATUS; the done flag is bit 0.
spec_facts: STATUS bit 0 is DONE, bit 1 is ERR; both are write-1-to-clear.
The caller's note that ERR is bit 2 is wrong.
items.fn_signature: pub fn clear_error<B: RegBus>(bus: &mut B) -> Result<(), SpecGap>

items.task_prompt: Write `start_transfer`: program the address and length, start the engine, then wait for DONE in STATUS.
spec_facts: ADDR is at 0x40 and LEN at 0x44; both must be written before GO.
items.fn_signature: pub fn start_transfer<B: RegBus>(bus: &mut B, addr: u32, len: u32) -> Result<(), SpecGap>
